<a id="search-and-discovery"></a>

# Search and Discovery

`find` is the read-only discovery surface. It searches one registered book with `--book` or all registered books with `--all` in registry order. An open book is read from its extracted state and a closed book from its container, so a search never requires `book open`.

The match mode defaults to `literal`. `--mode glob` matches `*`, `?` and `\` against the whole line or title, and `--mode regex` accepts a Go regular expression. `--ignore-case` folds case in every mode, and `--word` limits literal matching to letter, digit and underscore boundaries. Every hit carries byte offsets and rune columns, so a caller can edit the exact span without searching again.

`--field` selects the text sources: `title` for node titles, `body` for node-placed blocks, `layout` for stored asciiui specifications, and `prose`, `note` and `footer` for region blocks. `all` selects every source. Generated RepoLayout bodies and rendered drawings are never searched, so a result always points at source text.

Scope filters narrow a search without a second query. `--node <id>` covers a node and its whole subtree, `--block <id>` covers one placed block and its notes, and `--kind`, `--type`, `--status`, `--part` and `--locked` or `--unlocked` select by metadata. A filter that names an unknown node or block is rejected with `search.unknown-id`.

`--result` chooses the shape of the answer: `matches` lists one item per matching line, `blocks`, `nodes` and `books` aggregate the same hits, and `count` reports only totals plus the distinct book, block and node counts. `--limit` and `--offset` page the result items while `count` and `occurrences` stay complete. `--count` is the compatibility alias for `--result count`.

JSON is the default output. Schema version 2 adds spans, the effective scope and the submitted query to the result. `--format ndjson` streams a meta line, the items, any warnings and a summary, and `--text` prints a human summary. A missing body is a warning (`search.missing-body`), an unreadable book in `--all` is a warning (`search.read-failed`), and `--strict` turns every warning into a failure.

`--query` is repeatable: up to eight queries combine with `--join or` by default or `--join and`. The join unit follows the result mode: a line or title for `matches` and `count`, a block, node or book for the group modes. `--query-mode` aligns by index and allows mixed modes, including `fuzzy`; with several queries every span carries its query index and group items add `perQuery` counters.

`--fuzzy 1` to `--fuzzy 3` enables typo-tolerant literal matching: every query word must match a distinct word on the line within the edit distance, in query order. Punctuation separates words, a span carries its `distance`, and `--word` cannot be combined with fuzzy.

Path and reference filters complete the metadata filters: `--node-path` matches a glob against the title path, `--book-path` restricts `--all` by output path, `--ref` selects blocks whose text references an ID and `--missing-body` selects blocks without a body. Without a query, a filter-only request lists the matching blocks, nodes, books or counts.

`--group-by` and `--count-by` aggregate by `type`, `status`, `kind` or `part`; keys sort case-insensitively and a group reports its first line, count and occurrences. `--require-match` exits 1 with `search.no-match` when the payload is empty, and `--snapshot` holds a shared book lock for a consistent read.

`pecia index build --all --write` writes the derived search index; `index status` reports `missing`, `fresh`, `stale`, `corrupt` or `open`, and `index clear --write` removes it. The index is keyed by a container fingerprint and only covers closed books. `--index auto` uses a fresh index when the query can be served from its postings and scans otherwise, `--index force` rejects a missing or stale index and an unsupported query, and `--verify` re-checks indexed lines against the source.

The JSON schema adds `queries`, `join`, `fuzzy`, `index` and `perQuery` to describe the request and the index decision; each span carries `query` and `distance`, and each match carries `file`, the rendered path. `--format ndjson` streams `meta`, `match`, `group`, `warning` and `summary` lines. Exit codes stay 0 success, 1 failure (including `--require-match`), 2 usage and 3 rejected.

Search is also the audit tool for the rendered corpus. One regex sweep across every field finds stray terms without opening a book: `pecia find --all --mode regex --field all --query "term-a|term-b" --result matches`. Every match reports `file`, the rendered path such as `Docs/clabok/migrations.md` or `README.md`, next to `bookPath`, `node` and `block`, so a hit can be opened and fixed directly. `--result count` answers presence questions. `--index auto` is the practical default for audits; `--index force` requires a fresh index for every searched book, while a stale index falls back to a scan.
